title: Natural tensor comparison for associated-sheaf stalks
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme], and let $x\in X$. Put $B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and let $\rho:A\to B$ be the canonical germ homomorphism. Write $S(M)=\widetilde M_x$ for the stalk of the associated sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections, def-pc-module-stalk-functor], as a $B$-module, and $U$ for restriction of scalars along $\rho$. There exists an isomorphism of bifunctors from $\operatorname{Mod}(B)\times\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ to $\operatorname{Mod}(A)$, with components $U(N\otimes_B S(M))\cong U(N)\otimes_A M$, natural in both $B$-module $N$ and $A$-module $M$. No flatness, acyclicity or boundedness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Construct each component directly using IsBaseChange.tensorEquiv N, restricted to A, and convert the resulting linear equivalence to a ModuleCat isomorphism. Its inverse on pure tensors is n tensor m ↦ n tensor germ(m), as verified using cancelBaseChange_symm_tmul. This uses only proved Mathlib declarations; no existence witness is chosen.

proof.text: For naturality in M, compute the stalk map on the germ of the global section corresponding to m. stalkFunctor_map_germ_apply and tilde.toOpen_map_app give S(f)(germ(m)) = germ(f(m)). Thus the inverse component commutes with tensoring f, by TensorProduct.ext'. For naturality in N, the inverse formula on pure tensors immediately commutes with g tensor identity. NatIso.ofComponents first assembles the isomorphism in M and then in N; invert it to get the stated orientation.

lean.statement:
theorem nonempty_restrictScalars_tensor_tildeStalkNatIso
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (x : Spec (.of A)) :
    let S := tilde.functor (.of A) ⋙
      RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace x
    let U := ModuleCat.restrictScalars (StructureSheaf.toStalk A x).hom
    Nonempty
      ((Functor.postcompose₂.obj U).obj
        ((((Functor.whiskeringLeft₂ _).obj (𝟭 _)).obj S).obj (curriedTensor _)) ≅
      (((Functor.whiskeringLeft₂ _).obj U).obj (𝟭 _)).obj (curriedTensor _))
